mlh-fellowship.about:
The MLH Fellowship is described by its organiser as a fully remote, 12-week internship alternative. Fellows learn to collaborate on open-source projects with peers and engineers from partner companies, across tracks such as software engineering, site reliability and blockchain.

Fellows receive an educational stipend. The main page does not publish detailed eligibility rules, countries or cohort dates; these are in the FAQ and application form.
mlh-fellowship.eligibility: The main page does not state eligibility rules, age limits or countries. Check the Fellowship FAQ and application form before applying.
how_to_apply: Open the MLH Fellowship page
Choose the track you want
Submit the application for the upcoming start date
Complete any interview or technical steps requested
mlh-fellowship.costs: Free to apply; fellows receive an educational stipend (amount not stated on the page).

nasa-ostem-internships-summer-2027.about:
NASA OSTEM internships place students with NASA scientists and engineers on real projects. The summer session lasts ten weeks; sessions in fall and spring also exist. Applications go through NASA STEM Gateway.

The official page states U.S. citizenship is required for both OSTEM internships and Pathways, with an age minimum of 18 at the session start and a 3.0 GPA; high-school seniors can apply for the summer right after graduating.

It is listed here so students know the programme and its limits: students who are not US citizens cannot apply and should look at other agencies' programmes (such as ESA or CERN).
nasa-ostem-internships-summer-2027.eligibility: U.S. citizens only; the official page states citizenship is required and describes no path for non-citizens (so citizens of Georgia, Qatar and other countries cannot apply unless they hold US citizenship). At least 18 years old by session start; GPA 3.0 on a 4.0 scale; enrolled part- or full-time in an accredited programme, or a high-school senior applying for summer.
how_to_apply: Create a profile on NASA STEM Gateway
Complete the profile and upload transcript and resume
Search OSTEM opportunities and apply to up to the allowed number of projects
Submit before 1 March 2027, 11:59 p.m. EST
Await mentor selection
nasa-ostem-internships-summer-2027.costs: No fee. Interns receive a stipend; relocation and housing are the intern's responsibility for on-site placements.

nato-internship-programme.about:
NATO interns work full-time (38 hours a week) in divisions across the International Staff, supporting policy, defence planning, public diplomacy, legal and administrative work. The stipend is EUR 1,335 a month (2026), adjusted yearly, with a prepaid return economy ticket of up to EUR 1,200 and 15 days of paid leave.

The online application opens each April-May; final selections are made between July and September, with starts in March or September of the following year. The most recent deadline was 30 April 2026. SHAPE in Mons and the Allied commands run their own internship calls.
nato-internship-programme.eligibility: Citizen of a NATO member country (Georgia and Qatar are not members, so not eligible); at least 21; two years of university study and enrolled in the third year, or highest degree obtained under a year ago, or enrolled in master or PhD. Proficiency in English or French.
how_to_apply: Watch nato.int for the annual call (spring).
Register and complete the online form with CV and motivation.
Selection runs July to September.
Start in March or September of the following year.
nato-internship-programme.costs: EUR 1,335/month stipend (2026), return travel up to EUR 1,200, 15 days paid leave. No fee.

nims-internship-program.about:
NIMS, Japan's national materials-science institute, accepts current undergraduate and graduate students from domestic and international universities as interns under a host researcher. An internship lasts up to 90 consecutive calendar days within the fiscal year.

You find a host through the SAMURAI researcher directory, contact one researcher at a time, and email your application form, CV, enrolment certificate and transcripts; the researcher then forwards the documents. Direct submission to the office is not processed.

Selected students receive a daily allowance and accommodation fees (excluding utilities); students on MEXT, JSPS or JST scholarships must check with their sponsor. The next call is expected to open in December 2026.
nims-internship-program.eligibility: Currently enrolled undergraduate or graduate students at domestic or international universities (postdocs excluded). No nationality restriction stated; Georgian and Qatari students are not excluded. Holders of MEXT/JSPS/JST scholarships must confirm eligibility with their sponsor.
how_to_apply: Find a host researcher in the SAMURAI directory (samurai.nims.go.jp) and contact one at a time
Email the English application form, CV, enrolment certificate (issued within 3 months) and transcripts
If accepted, the researcher forwards your documents to the NIMS Graduate Program Section
Agree start and end dates with the researcher
nims-internship-program.costs: Daily allowance and accommodation fees (excluding utilities) are covered; transport is generally not.

nordplus-higher-education-student-mobili.about:
Nordplus Higher Education is one of the five Nordplus sub-programmes. Universities build networks and apply for funding; students then apply for exchange places through their own university's international office. The Nordplus site shows 1 February 2027 as the application deadline for institutions.

Students should ask their university whether it belongs to a Nordplus Higher Education network.
nordplus-higher-education-student-mobili.eligibility: Students at Nordic or Baltic universities that take part in a Nordplus Higher Education network.
how_to_apply: Ask your international office about Nordplus networks.
Apply in the university's student call.
Follow the host university's admission steps.
nordplus-higher-education-student-mobili.costs: Grants to participating institutions; mobility grants for students vary by project.

nordplus-junior-school-pupil-mobility.about:
Nordplus is the Nordic Council of Ministers' education programme with five sub-programmes: Junior, Higher Education, Adult, Horizontal and Nordic Languages. Nordplus Junior supports school-level mobility and partnerships in the Nordic-Baltic region.

Individual pupils do not apply directly: the school or institution applies with a project and then selects the pupils. The Nordplus site states an application deadline of 1 February 2027 for institutions' applications (check the exact call for the Junior sub-programme).
nordplus-junior-school-pupil-mobility.eligibility: Schools and institutions in the Nordic and Baltic countries apply; pupils join through their school.
how_to_apply: Ask your school whether it has a Nordplus Junior project.
The school finds partners and applies at nordplusonline.org.
Pupils are selected by the school.
nordplus-junior-school-pupil-mobility.costs: Grants for project and mobility costs paid to the applicant institution.

nvidia-ignite-internship-2027.about:
Ignite is NVIDIA's early-talent summer programme for current freshmen and sophomores, 12 weeks long. It gives students an early taste of working on GPU, AI and software products with a team.

NVIDIA states interns are employees with benefits. The page does not give pay or international rules, so check the posting for the office you target.
nvidia-ignite-internship-2027.eligibility: Current freshmen and sophomores in a BS programme. International rules and work authorisation: see the posting.
how_to_apply: Open NVIDIA University Recruiting and find Ignite postings
Submit CV and transcript on the NVIDIA careers portal
Complete interviews
nvidia-ignite-internship-2027.costs: Paid (interns are employees); amount not stated on the overview page.

nvidia-university-internship-2027.about:
NVIDIA hires interns year-round for engineering, research and other teams, with a minimum duration of 12 weeks. The company states its interns are employees and receive benefits.

Apply to roles that match your degree and location; the careers portal lists offices worldwide.
nvidia-university-internship-2027.eligibility: Students pursuing BS, MS, PhD or MBA degrees. Work authorisation for the posting's country is needed; see the posting.
how_to_apply: Search intern roles on the NVIDIA careers portal
Apply with CV and transcript
Complete technical interviews
nvidia-university-internship-2027.costs: Paid; amount varies by location and level.

opec-fund-internship-program.about:
The OPEC Fund Internship Program places students in departments across the institution, including public and private sector operations, finance, strategy, legal, HR and IT. Typical tasks are research, writing, organising information and supporting staff.

Applications for 2026 were collected through careers.opecfund.org with a CV, proof of enrolment or diploma, latest transcripts and a 150-250 word motivation statement in English. The call is repeated yearly, so watch the Internships page for the next one.
opec-fund-internship-program.eligibility: Age 19 to 25. Enrolled in an undergraduate programme (having completed at least two years) or a graduate programme, or graduated no more than one year before the deadline. All nationalities may apply; nationals of OPEC Fund member countries (Algeria, Ecuador, Gabon, Indonesia, Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Libya, Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Venezuela) are strongly encouraged. Fluent English required; Arabic, French, German or Spanish is an advantage. Proficiency in Microsoft 365. Work or study permit rules for Austria are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Watch the OPEC Fund Internships page for the next annual call
Prepare CV, enrolment letter or diploma, latest transcripts and a 150-250 word English motivation statement
Apply through the OPEC Fund careers portal
Interns are placed by interest and departmental needs
opec-fund-internship-program.costs: The page does not mention a stipend; check the call text for pay details.

osce-internship-programme.about:
The OSCE, the world's largest regional security organisation, takes interns into its Secretariat, institutions and field operations for two to six months, full-time. Areas include politico-military affairs, economic and environmental affairs, human rights and communications.

Internships are generally unpaid with no travel reimbursement, though some interns who are not Vienna residents may receive a living-cost allowance. Interns arrange their own health insurance and, where needed, a D-visa (the OSCE can provide a support letter).
osce-internship-programme.eligibility: Final-year graduate/postgraduate student or graduate within two years (older pages say one year); upper age about 30; fluent English. Nationals of OSCE participating States or Partners for Co-operation (Georgia is a participating State; Qatari citizens should check the vacancy for partner-state eligibility).
how_to_apply: Search internship vacancies on jobs.osce.org.
Apply online with CV and motivation letter.
Provide proof of enrolment or graduation.
Arrange insurance and visa after selection.
osce-internship-programme.costs: Generally unpaid; limited living-cost allowance for some Vienna interns. Insurance at intern's cost.

peggy-guggenheim-collection-internationa.about:
The museum's International Internship Program takes students and recent graduates into departments such as curatorial, education and communications. General applicants send a CV and a one-page cover letter explaining their interest, plus availability, to the museum's internship email.

Italian students apply through partner universities for credit. Interns are generally unpaid; the Anita Belgiorno-Nettis scholarship gives EUR 1,500 to one Australian candidate each year.
peggy-guggenheim-collection-internationa.eligibility: University students and recent graduates; good English; Italian helpful. Non-EU applicants must arrange their own visa.
how_to_apply: Read the how-to-apply and FAQ pages
Write a one-page cover letter
Email CV, letter and availability to the museum internship address
Or apply via your university if it is a partner
peggy-guggenheim-collection-internationa.costs: Unpaid; interns cover travel and living costs. EUR 1,500 scholarship for one Australian candidate yearly.

pg-internships.about:
P&G runs internships worldwide, lasting from six weeks to 12 months depending on location and format (in person, virtual or both). You do not need a specific major or prior experience.

The company describes internships as the route for students ready to start a career and recommends its student programmes for a lighter introduction. Pay is competitive but not published.

Search the global internships page, pick your country's posting and apply online; start and end dates are on each posting.
pg-internships.eligibility: University students; no specific major or experience required; work authorisation depends on the country of the posting (not stated on the global page).
how_to_apply: Open the P&G global internships page
Choose the posting for your country
Apply online and complete the assessments and interviews

riken-cbs-summer-program-2027.about:
The RIKEN CBS Summer Program offers motivated students from around the world a hands-on stay in one of Japan's leading neuroscience institutes. Plan A is an eight-week research internship in a CBS lab (8 June to 5 August 2027); Plan B is a five-day lecture course (5 to 9 July 2027); applicants can select both on one form.

Participation is fully on-site. Interns live in RIKEN I-House in Wako, and RIKEN pays accommodation and round-trip airfare for approved applicants (costs are reimbursed after returning home).

Applicants submit a CV, a roughly 500-word motivation letter and, for Plan A, a project description; a supervisor uploads a recommendation letter.
riken-cbs-summer-program-2027.eligibility: Anyone beyond high-school level who is enrolled at a university or company when applying and remains enrolled throughout (gap-year applicants need an enrolment certificate from their future institution). High-school students cannot apply. Must attend the whole programme on site; non-Japanese nationals need a valid passport and arrange their own visa. No nationality restriction is stated, so Georgian and Qatari students may apply.
how_to_apply: Choose Plan A, Plan B or both
Prepare a CV, a motivation letter (about 500 words) and, for Plan A, a project description; add a financial-support letter if you need funding
Submit the online form by 8 January 2027, 9:00 JST (no saved drafts)
Ask your academic supervisor to upload the recommendation letter
Results are sent around mid-February
riken-cbs-summer-program-2027.costs: No fee. RIKEN covers accommodation and round-trip airfare for approved applicants; visa costs are the participant's.

rolls-royce-discover-behind-the-scenes-2.about:
Discover: Behind-the-Scenes is a 4-day in-person work-experience programme with a group project, for specific school year groups (Year 11-13, S4-6) at Derby, Solihull, Bristol and Inchinnan between November 2026 and August 2027.

The page states no nationality requirement, but you must attend in person for all four days; accommodation is not provided and only a small travel bursary is offered. Rolls-Royce helps accepted students obtain school permission.

Inchinnan applications are open via Workday; for the other cohorts join the Emerging Talent pool for opening alerts.
rolls-royce-discover-behind-the-scenes-2.eligibility: School students in the specified year groups (Year 11, 12, 13 or S4-6 depending on the cohort); no nationality rule stated, but attendance in the UK for all four days is required and Rolls-Royce does not cover accommodation.
how_to_apply: Choose the cohort matching your year group and site
Apply through the Rolls-Royce Workday portal when it opens (Inchinnan is open now)
Join the Emerging Talent pool for notifications
rolls-royce-discover-behind-the-scenes-2.costs: Free to attend; unpaid; accommodation not covered; small travel bursary available.

rolls-royce-internships-global.about:
Rolls-Royce lists student and graduate opportunities outside the UK and US for China, Singapore, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Canada, Poland and Oman. In Germany it offers mandatory and voluntary internships, thesis placements and working-student positions; the US offers 12-week summer internships and co-ops for bachelor's students with a 3.0 GPA (US roles may require US citizenship).

UK internships can only progress UK nationals (or MoD-approved dual nationals), so international students should target the other countries.

Pick your country on the careers site, apply for the posting and join the Talent Community for alerts. The process is an online application, then phone or in-person assessment and offer. No openings were showing on the pages checked on 14 Nov 2026.
rolls-royce-internships-global.eligibility: University students; UK roles require UK nationality; US roles may require US citizenship and 3.0 GPA; other countries follow local rules stated in each posting.
how_to_apply: Open the global students and graduates page
Choose your country and search Intern roles
Apply online and join the Talent Community for alerts
Complete phone/in-person assessment
rolls-royce-internships-global.costs: Paid placements; amounts set per posting.

seeds-of-peace-international-camp.about:
The Seeds of Peace website lists its International Camp, Youth Leadership, Alumni (GATHER) and Educators programmes, and says its alumni work in 27 countries. Participants are selected through partner organisations in the regions where the programme works, not by open global application.

The public page does not state ages, cost or deadlines; see 'Become a Seed' (seedsofpeace.org/getinvolved/become-a-seed/) or contact info@seedsofpeace.org.
seeds-of-peace-international-camp.eligibility: Teenagers from partner regions, selected by local partner organisations; the public page gives no precise age or eligibility rules.
how_to_apply: Read the 'Become a Seed' page on the Seeds of Peace site.
Ask the Seeds of Peace team (info@seedsofpeace.org) whether your region has a selection process.
Follow the partner's selection steps.
seeds-of-peace-international-camp.costs: Not stated on the opened page; typically funded for selected participants; confirm with the organiser.

shape-nato-internship-programme.about:
SHAPE, NATO's strategic military headquarters in Mons, runs its own internship programme separate from the NATO HQ scheme in Brussels. Interns support branches such as legal, strategic communications, policy, logistics and cyber.

The 2027 intake closed on 28 February 2026; the call for the 2028 intake had not been dated as of November 2026, with updates expected in October to November. Check the SHAPE candidates page for the opening date and exact stipend.
shape-nato-internship-programme.eligibility: Nationals of NATO member countries (Georgia and Qatar not eligible); students or recent graduates, English or French. Check the SHAPE candidates page for age and study requirements.
how_to_apply: Watch the SHAPE internships page for the 2028 call.
Register and apply online with CV and motivation.
Selection runs over the following months.
Placement starts in 2028.
shape-nato-internship-programme.costs: See current SHAPE call for stipend and travel; interns are responsible for housing in Mons.

shopify-engineering-internship-2027.about:
Engineering interns at Shopify build commerce tools on real teams. Shopify is remote-first and lists remote roles for several regions; which regions accept interns is stated on internships.shopify.com.

Shopify also runs Dev Degree (earn-while-you-learn, Canada) and apprenticeships for design and product.
shopify-engineering-internship-2027.eligibility: Students in software engineering; regional and work-authorisation rules are on the internship site. Confirm before applying.
how_to_apply: Open internships.shopify.com
Choose your region
Apply with CV and complete interviews
shopify-engineering-internship-2027.costs: Paid; amount not stated on the overview page.

smithsonian-internships.about:
The Smithsonian offers internships in its museums, libraries, archives and research centres. Each unit runs its own listings, terms and deadlines, and applications are generally made through the Smithsonian online academic appointment system.

Many internships are paid by stipend, though some programmes (for example Office of Sponsored Projects internships) are unpaid. Read the individual listing for pay and requirements.
smithsonian-internships.eligibility: Varies by unit; generally students and recent graduates. Check each listing for nationality, visa and year-of-study rules.
how_to_apply: Browse internship listings on the Smithsonian fellowships and internships site
Choose a unit and term
Apply through the Smithsonian online application system with CV and statement
Meet the unit's deadline
smithsonian-internships.costs: Stipend where offered; amounts vary by unit.

smithsonian-nmnh-high-school-internship.about:
The NMNH High School Internship Program places students in museum departments in summer. The 2026 rules limited it to current high-school students aged 14-18 living in commuting distance of the museum in D.C., Maryland or Virginia; the official page says details for summer 2027 will be posted in early December 2026.

Applications go through the Smithsonian Online Academic Appointment System (SOLAA) with a resume, a statement of interest and one recommendation. This record is based on the official programme page as summarised in search results; its page blocks automated access, so confirm details and dates directly.
smithsonian-nmnh-high-school-internship.eligibility: 2026 rule: current high-school students aged 14-18 who live within commuting distance of the museum (D.C., Maryland, Virginia). 2027 rules to be posted in December 2026.
how_to_apply: Check the NMNH page in early December 2026
Apply through SOLAA with resume and statement of interest
Obtain one recommendation letter
smithsonian-nmnh-high-school-internship.costs: Pay not confirmed on the sources read; check the 2027 page.

snb-internships.about:
The SNB offers internships in areas such as economics, IT and other fields, where graduates contribute their own expertise. Internships typically last 12 months.

Vacancies are posted on the SNB careers portal. Interns are typically graduates with a bachelor's or master's degree; economics and data science are especially sought, and business administration and social sciences are considered in some cases.
snb-internships.eligibility: Typically graduates with a bachelor's or master's degree, good academic performance, language skills (not specified). The page states nothing about nationality or work permits; non-EU/EFTA nationals should check the posting and Swiss permit rules.
how_to_apply: Open careers.snb.ch
Find a current internship posting
Apply online via the Apply now link
snb-internships.costs: Pay is not stated on the page; check the posting.

spotify-summer-internship-2027.about:
Spotify's summer internship runs for 10 weeks from June to August in the London, Stockholm or New York offices; remote participation is not offered. Applications go only through Spotify's official jobs site.

The 2027 timeline was still 'coming soon' when checked. Spotify does not offer internships for high-school students.
spotify-summer-internship-2027.eligibility: Students in their graduating or penultimate year in an associate's, bachelor's, master's or PhD programme, or a bootcamp certificate. Work-permit rules depend on the office. Not for high-school students.
how_to_apply: Wait for the 2027 recruitment to open on lifeatspotify.com
Apply to the internship role in your office
Complete the interview stages
spotify-summer-internship-2027.costs: Paid; amount not stated on the page.

st-jude-hs-research-immersion-2027.about:
The High School Research Immersion places students in St. Jude research labs for eight weeks, roughly 40 hours a week (9am-5pm), ending with a community exhibition on 24 July 2027. The stipend is USD 4,800.

It is limited to US citizens, non-citizen nationals and permanent residents who are current juniors at a high school in the Memphis-Shelby County area or nearby Tennessee, Mississippi and Arkansas counties, aged 16+, with a 3.0 GPA. The page is inconsistent on 'rising seniors' vs 'current junior'; confirm with immersion@stjude.org.
st-jude-hs-research-immersion-2027.eligibility: US citizen, non-citizen national or permanent resident; current junior at a high school in the Memphis-Shelby County area or nearby TN/MS/AR counties; 16+; GPA 3.0+. Not open to international applicants.
how_to_apply: Complete the online application via 'Apply now'
Get a teacher recommendation submitted by 4 Dec 2026
If selected, provide guardian permission and official transcript

ubs-internship-program-switzerland.about: Structured internship for students who have completed at least four semesters. Applicants should expect online assessments that depend on the business area and must be completed within seven days of the invitation.
ubs-internship-program-switzerland.eligibility: At least four completed semesters and on track for a Swiss grade of 4.5 or equivalent. Non-EU/EFTA applicants need a permit; check the page.
how_to_apply: Open the official programme page and check which offices and divisions are recruiting for your graduation year.
Prepare a CV in English (and a cover letter if requested) and upload your transcript.
Submit the online application; you may be limited in how many divisions or offices you can apply to.
Complete the online assessments or recorded video interview within the window given in the invitation email.
Attend the interviews or assessment day; strong interns can receive a full-time return offer.

ubs-off-cycle-internship-program.about: Off-cycle internships run outside the summer cycle, typically for six months, and suit students taking a placement or gap period.
ubs-off-cycle-internship-program.eligibility: University students; check the page for year-of-study and right-to-work rules.
how_to_apply: Open the official programme page and check which offices and divisions are recruiting for your graduation year.
Prepare a CV in English (and a cover letter if requested) and upload your transcript.
Submit the online application; you may be limited in how many divisions or offices you can apply to.
Complete the online assessments or recorded video interview within the window given in the invitation email.
Attend the interviews or assessment day; strong interns can receive a full-time return offer.

ubs-summer-internship-program.about:
Students starting their second-to-last year can apply for UBS summer internships; no finance degree is required. Internships start in June (December in Australia and New Zealand).

Limits apply: up to three applications in APAC and the US/Canada per year, and one UK plus one EMEA programme.
ubs-summer-internship-program.eligibility: APAC: second-to-last year, under two years' work experience; UK/EMEA: on track for a 2:1 or equivalent; US/Canada: GPA 3.2+. Right to work in the chosen country.
how_to_apply: Open the official programme page and check which offices and divisions are recruiting for your graduation year.
Prepare a CV in English (and a cover letter if requested) and upload your transcript.
Submit the online application; you may be limited in how many divisions or offices you can apply to.
Complete the online assessments or recorded video interview within the window given in the invitation email.
Attend the interviews or assessment day; strong interns can receive a full-time return offer.

ubs-tomorrows-talent-spring-insight.about: UBS's Spring Insight programme introduces students early in their studies to its divisions and can lead to fast-track access to summer internships.
ubs-tomorrows-talent-spring-insight.eligibility: Students in the early years of their degree; check the programme page for year of study and right-to-work conditions.
how_to_apply: Open the programme page.
Apply online with CV.
Complete assessments.
Attend the programme week.
ubs-tomorrows-talent-spring-insight.costs: Unpaid programme; check page for expenses.

umap-commtech-camp-insight-2027-indonesi.about: The UMAP home page features CommTECH Camp Insight 2027 in Indonesia as open to 50 international participants and requiring no specific technical or practical background. The camp is part of UMAP's Discovery Camp series. The page does not give exact dates, price or deadline, so check the UMAP programme database (usco2.umap.org) or ask the organising university. The map pin uses Jakarta as a placeholder.
umap-commtech-camp-insight-2027-indonesi.eligibility: International participants; the page does not state age or study level beyond UMAP's university focus. Check the programme database.
how_to_apply: Open umap.org and follow the CommTECH Camp Insight 2027 link.
Check dates, cost and application on the programme database.
Apply through your university or directly if the camp allows.
umap-commtech-camp-insight-2027-indonesi.costs: Not stated on the page; check the programme database.

umap-student-exchange-asia-pacific.about:
UMAP offers semester programmes, short-term programmes, virtual exchanges, Collaborative Online International Learning (COIL) and Discovery Camp. Students normally take part via their home university if it is a UMAP member; the UMAP programme database (usco2.umap.org) lists programmes.

Eligibility is set by each member university; the main page does not state general student rules. The map pin shows a nominal location; hosts are spread across the Asia-Pacific.
umap-student-exchange-asia-pacific.eligibility: Students of UMAP member institutions; rules are set by each member university.
how_to_apply: Check whether your university is a UMAP member on umap.org.
Browse the programme database (usco2.umap.org).
Apply through your university's international office.
umap-student-exchange-asia-pacific.costs: Varies by programme and member university.

un-escap-internship-programme.about:
ESCAP is the UN development arm for Asia and the Pacific, with more than 50 member states. Interns work in divisions such as Trade, Social Development, Macroeconomic Policy, Energy and ICT for two to six months, with no extension beyond six.

Internships are unpaid; the intern or sponsoring institution handles travel, visa, housing and living costs. Apply to individual vacancies via the UN Careers portal or ESCAP's website.
un-escap-internship-programme.eligibility: In or having completed a graduate programme, or enrolled in or completed the final year of a first university degree. English proficiency. Open to all nationalities, including Georgia and Qatar (Georgia is an ESCAP member; Qatar too).
how_to_apply: Review current internship vacancies on the ESCAP internships page.
Apply via the UN Careers portal.
Submit CV, cover letter and academic proof.
Arrange visa and costs if selected.
un-escap-internship-programme.costs: Unpaid; all costs borne by the intern or sponsor.

un-secretariat-internship-programme.about:
The Secretariat internship programme lets students and recent graduates work for 2 to 6 months in a department or office of the UN Secretariat, from policy and legal work to communications and administration. Interns are placed in New York, Geneva, Vienna, Nairobi, Bangkok, Addis Ababa, Santiago, Beirut and other duty stations, and some roles can be done remotely.

Internships are unpaid: the intern or their sponsoring institution pays for travel, visa, insurance and living costs. Candidates apply to individual internship vacancies on the UN Careers portal (Inspira successor), choosing the department and location themselves.

The UN charges no fee at any stage of recruitment. An internship does not guarantee later employment, but it is the most common first step into the UN system.
un-secretariat-internship-programme.eligibility: Enrolled in (or graduated within the past year from) a bachelor, master or PhD programme, with a start date before or within one year of graduation. Strong English or French. Not a child or sibling of a UN Secretariat staff member. Open to all nationalities, including citizens of Georgia and Qatar; applicants must arrange their own visa.
how_to_apply: Create a profile on the UN Careers portal (careers.un.org).
Search "Internship" job openings by department and duty station.
Submit CV, cover letter and proof of enrolment or graduation for each vacancy.
If shortlisted, complete the interview and provide university documents.
Arrange visa, insurance and housing yourself before the start date.
un-secretariat-internship-programme.costs: No stipend or travel support from the UN; interns or sponsoring institutions pay for travel, visa, health insurance, accommodation and living costs. No application fee.

un-women-internship-programme.about:
UN Women places interns in its headquarters and field offices for two to six months, generally full-time and throughout the year. Applications go through UN Women's careers site, filtered to internships; incomplete forms can be disqualified.

Interns are not salaried. A stipend for basic daily expenses may be provided only if no other body is funding you; you or your sponsor cover travel, insurance and accommodation. The page does not mention remote placements, so check each posting.
un-women-internship-programme.eligibility: Enrolled in a master's, post-master's or doctoral programme, or in the final year of a bachelor's degree (or equivalent); recent graduates who can start within two years of graduating. The page states no nationality restriction. Selected candidates must supply two recommendation letters, health insurance, proof of enrolment or graduation and passport/visa.
how_to_apply: Search internships on the UN Women Careers website with the internship filter
Complete every section of the online application (a CV or P11 does not replace the fields)
If selected, send two recommendation letters, proof of health insurance, proof of enrolment or graduation and a scanned passport
Sign the internship offer and agreement
un-women-internship-programme.costs: Unpaid; a stipend for meals and local transport is only possible if you have no other funding. Travel, insurance and accommodation are at your own or your sponsor's expense.

undp-internship-programme.about:
UNDP internships place students and recent graduates in headquarters, regional hubs and country offices worldwide, and some are remote. Interns support teams on development policy, governance, climate and environment, crisis response, data and communications.

Unless sponsored by another institution or government, interns are eligible for a flat monthly stipend that depends on the country of assignment and whether the internship is in-person or remote. Travel and other costs are the intern's responsibility.

Vacancies are advertised on the UNDP jobs site throughout the year; you apply to each separately.
undp-internship-programme.eligibility: Final-year undergraduate, postgraduate or PhD student, or a recent graduate starting within one year of graduation. Working knowledge of English (or the office language). Open to all nationalities, including Georgia and Qatar. Not open to close relatives of UNDP staff.
how_to_apply: Browse internship vacancies on jobs.undp.org.
Select the office and project that match your studies.
Submit CV and motivation letter online.
Provide proof of enrolment or graduation if shortlisted.
undp-internship-programme.costs: Monthly stipend by duty station; travel, visa and housing are the intern's responsibility. No fee.

unep-internship-programme.about:
UNEP, the UN's environmental authority, hosts interns at its Nairobi headquarters and offices worldwide. As part of the UN Secretariat system, internships are unpaid; UNEP offices state that the UN provides no financial support, so interns arrange travel and living costs.

Interns are typically in the third or fourth year of an undergraduate or graduate programme (some offices need a graduate-level enrolment). Placement lasts 2 to 6 months. Apply through UN Careers/Inspira, selecting UNEP internship vacancies.
unep-internship-programme.eligibility: Enrolled in or recently graduated from a first or graduate degree (third/fourth-year undergraduates accepted by some offices); English proficiency; open to all nationalities including Georgia and Qatar. No children or siblings of UN staff.
how_to_apply: Create a profile on UN Careers.
Search UNEP internship vacancies (Nairobi).
Apply with CV and motivation.
Arrange visa and costs yourself if selected.
unep-internship-programme.costs: Unpaid; the intern or sponsor covers all costs.

unesco-internship-programme.about:
UNESCO runs two internship rounds a year (January and July). Interns join sectors such as Education, Natural Sciences, Culture, Communication, or corporate services at Paris headquarters or field offices.

Interns are not paid and cover their own travel, visa and insurance, though they receive paid leave days and limited workplace insurance. Placement is not guaranteed, and your application stays in the portal for six months. You have only one hour to finish the application form once you start, so prepare your documents first.

Separate sponsored traineeships exist; apply for those only through the sponsoring entity.
unesco-internship-programme.eligibility: At least 20 years old; enrolled in the third or final year of a bachelor, or a graduate programme, or graduated within 12 months of the start date (check the vacancy). Excellent English or French. Open to all UNESCO Member State nationals, including Georgia and Qatar.
how_to_apply: Open the UNESCO careers portal and find internship vacancies.
Prepare CV and motivation letter in advance.
Complete the application within the one-hour limit.
Wait for contact; applications stay active six months.
unesco-internship-programme.costs: Unpaid; travel, visa, health insurance and living costs borne by the intern. No fee.

unhcr-internship-programme.about:
UNHCR places students and recent graduates in protection, legal, programme, data, communications and operations teams for two to six months, extendable to eight (full-time) or twelve (part-time). Many roles can also be remote.

Pay is not uniform: UNHCR pages note an allowance toward food, local transport and living costs for interns without outside support, while some regional postings are explicitly unpaid. Always read the terms of the specific vacancy. Interns pay for travel and visas.

Applications are made through UNHCR vacancy postings; the programme is competitive but open to all nationalities.
unhcr-internship-programme.eligibility: Current student at an accredited institution with at least two years of undergraduate study, or a graduate within the past two years. English at B2 or higher. No close relatives among UNHCR staff. Open to all nationalities, including Georgia and Qatar; visas are the intern's responsibility.
how_to_apply: Find open internship vacancies on the UNHCR careers page.
Check the office, duration and whether an allowance is offered.
Apply online with CV and cover letter.
Provide proof of enrolment or graduation if selected.
unhcr-internship-programme.costs: Allowance varies by office and may be absent; travel and visa costs borne by the intern. No fee.

unicef-internship-programme.about:
UNICEF offers interns hands-on work in child protection, education, health, nutrition, policy, communications, data and operations. Placements run 6 to 26 weeks, full- or part-time, at headquarters (New York) and in regional and country offices worldwide.

Interns receive a monthly stipend, and UNICEF may add a one-time lump sum toward travel and visa costs when funds allow; it also supplies documents for visa applications. Opportunities are posted year-round on the UNICEF jobs portal, filtered for internships.

Only shortlisted candidates are contacted, so tailor your profile to each vacancy.
unicef-internship-programme.eligibility: At least 18; enrolled in an undergraduate, graduate or PhD programme, or graduated within the past two years. Proficiency in English, French or Spanish (sometimes the local working language). No immediate relatives employed by UNICEF. Open to all nationalities; Georgian and Qatari citizens may apply.
how_to_apply: Open the UNICEF jobs portal and filter vacancies for "Internship".
Choose a role and location that match your studies.
Click Apply and tailor your profile, CV and motivation to the vacancy.
Only shortlisted candidates are contacted for interview.
unicef-internship-programme.costs: Monthly stipend by duty station; one-time travel/visa lump sum possible when funding allows. No application fee.

unilever-internships.about:
Unilever describes its internships as hands-on placements alongside experienced experts on real business challenges. They sit alongside the Unilever Future Leaders' Programme for graduates and apprenticeships.

The central page does not give duration, eligibility or pay; these are set on each country's early-careers page (listed markets include the UK and Ireland, Germany, the Netherlands, Taiwan, India, Egypt, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Indonesia and Argentina).

Join the talent network for alerts, then apply to the posting in your country.
unilever-internships.eligibility: University students; requirements (year of study, work permit, language) are set per country page and are not stated centrally.
how_to_apply: Open the Unilever early careers page
Select your country's early-careers page
Join the talent network for alerts and apply to the internship posting
unilever-internships.costs: Pay is set by country; not published on the central page.

university-of-auckland-summer-research-s.about:
Summer Research Scholarships pair an undergraduate with a University of Auckland supervisor on a research project during the New Zealand summer. The 2026/27 scholarship pays a tax-free stipend of NZD 6,820.80 in fortnightly instalments over 10 weeks, starting 1 December.

The scheme is open to high-achieving domestic and international students currently enrolled at a New Zealand university who will have completed at least two years of full-time equivalent undergraduate study. Students browse the summer research project list by faculty and contact supervisors once projects are live.

It does not recruit students from overseas universities: international students must already be enrolled in New Zealand.
university-of-auckland-summer-research-s.eligibility: Domestic and international students currently enrolled at a New Zealand university, with at least two years of full-time-equivalent undergraduate study completed by December of the application year. Not open to students enrolled only overseas.
how_to_apply: Browse the summer research projects by faculty when they go live
Follow the 'How to apply' page of the Scholarships Office when the round opens
After an offer, accept it and contact your supervisor
Add your bank account in Student Services Online to be paid
university-of-auckland-summer-research-s.costs: No application fee stated; the scholarship pays a stipend and enrols you in SUMRESCH 301.

unodc-bangkok-full-time-internship.about:
UNODC fights drugs, organised crime, corruption and terrorism and supports criminal-justice reform. Its Bangkok Regional Office (ROSEAP) offers full-time internships to graduate-level students; the Vienna headquarters and other field offices run their own.

UNODC internships are unpaid and the intern or sponsor covers all costs. Candidates must be in graduate study, in the last year of a first degree or recently graduated (undergraduates with fewer than three years of study are not eligible; some offices want master's or PhD enrolment). Interns cannot apply for a Secretariat post for six months after.
unodc-bangkok-full-time-internship.eligibility: Graduate student, final-year undergraduate or recent graduate (some UNODC offices require master's or PhD enrolment; check the vacancy); English proficiency; open to all nationalities including Georgia and Qatar.
how_to_apply: Read the full-time internship page of the UNODC office.
Submit CV, cover letter and academic proof as instructed.
Wait for contact from the programme team.
Arrange visa and costs if selected.
unodc-bangkok-full-time-internship.costs: Unpaid; interns or sponsors cover travel, visa, insurance, accommodation and living costs.

wfp-internship-programme.about:
WFP, the world's largest humanitarian organisation, offers internships of two to eight months at headquarters in Rome, regional bureaux and country offices, in logistics, supply chain, nutrition, data, communications, finance and programme work.

The stipend is a contribution to basic subsistence tied to the assignment city, up to USD 1,000 a month, with medical and accident insurance. Accommodation, travel and visas are not covered.
wfp-internship-programme.eligibility: Enrolled in an undergraduate programme with at least two years completed, or a graduate within six months (having attended classes in the last 12 months); fluent English. Open to all nationalities, including Georgia and Qatar (check the vacancy).
how_to_apply: Browse internship vacancies on WFP careers.
Apply online with CV and motivation.
Provide proof of enrolment.
Arrange housing and visa at your own cost.
wfp-internship-programme.costs: Stipend up to USD 1,000/month; insurance covered; travel, visa and housing not covered.

who-internship-programme.about:
WHO interns contribute to technical units covering public health, health systems, emergencies, data and policy, in Geneva, in the six regional offices or in country offices. Internships are full-time and last 6 to 24 weeks.

Since 2020, eligible interns who need financial support can receive a living allowance, assessed from a Declaration of Interests form; WHO also provides medical and accident insurance. Past interns cannot apply again.

Apply only through vacancy notices on WHO Careers; positions are posted continuously.
who-internship-programme.eligibility: At least 20 years old; enrolled in a relevant university degree or completed one within the past 18 months; three years of full-time university study; fluency in a working language of the office. Must hold a passport from a WHO Member State (Georgia and Qatar are members). No relatives on WHO staff; former interns excluded.
how_to_apply: Browse internship vacancy notices on WHO Careers.
Prepare CV, motivation letter and university proof.
Apply through the Stellis system before the notice closes.
Complete the Declaration of Interests to be assessed for the allowance.
who-internship-programme.costs: Insurance provided; living allowance for eligible interns (see vacancy). Travel and accommodation not covered. No fee.

wikimedia-foundation-software-engineerin.about:
Interns join an engineering team in Product and Technology, work on a primary project with defined deliverables and are supported by a manager and mentor.

Open to graduates, non-graduates and career changers. The jobs page does not state pay, so confirm compensation in the posting before applying.
wikimedia-foundation-software-engineerin.eligibility: Graduates, non-graduates or career changers; check the posting for location and work-authorisation rules.
how_to_apply: Open the Wikimedia Foundation jobs page
Find the Software Engineering Internship 2027 posting
Apply as the posting instructs
wikimedia-foundation-software-engineerin.costs: Pay not stated on the jobs page; verify in the posting.

wilson-center-internships.about:
The Wilson Center offers part-time, paid internships to current, recent or returning undergraduate and graduate students, aligned with fall, spring and summer terms. Research Assistant and Staff Assistant tracks have separate applications and deadlines.

Interns may work remotely, in person or hybrid depending on the position. Questions: internship@wilsoncenter.org.
wilson-center-internships.eligibility: Current, recent or returning undergraduate and graduate students. The page does not address international students or US work authorisation; ask internship@wilsoncenter.org before applying from abroad. Interns are subject to the Hatch Act.
how_to_apply: Open the Wilson Center Internships page for the next term
Choose Research Assistant or Staff Assistant and use its application page
Email internship@wilsoncenter.org with questions
wilson-center-internships.costs: Paid; rate not stated on the page.

wipo-internship-programme.about:
WIPO, the UN agency for intellectual property, hosts interns in Geneva across IP law, global economic research, patents, brands, development and communications. Category I covers third/fourth-year undergraduates, recent bachelor graduates and first-year master's students; Category II covers master's graduates and students who have finished coursework.

The stipend is CHF 1,645 to 2,170 per month (reduced by university or government funding), and nationals of developing and least-developed countries living at home can claim up to CHF 1,500 in travel. WIPO helps with visas. WIPO also runs a Young Experts Program and a PCT fellowship.
wipo-internship-programme.eligibility: Students or graduates (bachelor within two years, or master's) with very good English and/or French; no formal age limit. Nationals of WIPO Member States (Georgia and Qatar are members).
how_to_apply: Open the WIPO internship page and read the categories.
Submit CV and cover letter to the roster.
Wait for a unit to select you.
Arrange visa (WIPO assists) and accommodation.
wipo-internship-programme.costs: Stipend CHF 1,645-2,170/month; travel up to CHF 1,500 for eligible developing-country nationals. No fee.

world-bank-group-pioneers-internship.about:
The WBG Pioneers programme brings talented students into the World Bank Group (World Bank, IFC, MIGA) to work on development economics, finance, climate, digital, social and operations projects. Interns earn a competitive hourly salary.

The spring/summer cycle follows a fixed pattern: applications January to February, assessment in February, interviews in March and selection in April. You may apply for up to three positions, with a 2-page CV, 1-page cover letter and proof of enrolment.

A fee-free university letter is needed where an internship carries no tuition fee.
world-bank-group-pioneers-internship.eligibility: Final-year undergraduate or master/PhD student; 0 to 6 years of work experience; fluent English; citizen of a World Bank Group member country (Georgia and Qatar are members). Proof of eligibility (transcript or enrolment letter) required.
how_to_apply: Watch the World Bank careers site for the January opening.
Search the Pioneers internship vacancies and choose up to three.
Upload a 2-page CV and 1-page cover letter plus proof of enrolment.
Complete the online assessment and interviews (Feb-Mar).
world-bank-group-pioneers-internship.costs: Paid hourly salary; visa sponsorship and relocation terms in the offer. No application fee.

world-bank-wbg-pioneers-internship.about:
WBG Pioneers places final-year undergraduates and master's/PhD students across the World Bank Group, with a competitive hourly salary. You may apply for up to three positions.

Required materials are a two-page CV, a one-page cover letter and proof of enrolment; no-fee internships need a university letter.
world-bank-wbg-pioneers-internship.eligibility: Final-year undergraduates or master's/PhD students; 0-6 years of work experience; fluent English; citizen of a World Bank Group member country.
how_to_apply: Wait for the application window (Jan-Feb for spring/summer).
Submit CV, cover letter and enrolment proof for up to three positions.
Longlist and online assessment.
Interviews and selection (spring: March-April).

wto-internship-programme.about:
The WTO takes postgraduate interns into divisions covering trade negotiations, dispute settlement, economic research and trade policy review. The general programme lasts up to six months with a CHF 60 daily allowance (weekends and holidays included); travel to Geneva is not covered.

Separate China WTO Accessions and China General programmes serve nationals of developing and least-developed members and accession candidates, with CHF 90 a day, economy airfare and a monthly insurance subsidy, up to 10 months. The doctoral support programme is currently on hold.

Apply via the WTO external jobs platform and, for the China programmes, email CV and motivation letter to the programme address.
wto-internship-programme.eligibility: General programme: nationals of a WTO member or acceptance-negotiating country, age 21+, relevant bachelor degree plus enrolment in or completion of a master (completed within two years). China programmes: nationals of developing/least-developed WTO members or observers, max age 30. Georgia and Qatar are WTO members. English, French or Spanish.
how_to_apply: Fill in the WTO internship application form on the external jobs platform.
For China programmes, email CV, motivation letter and form to the programme address.
Keep your application on the roster (valid one year).
If selected, arrange mandatory Swiss health insurance (China programmes get a subsidy).
wto-internship-programme.costs: CHF 60/day (general) or CHF 90/day plus airfare and CHF 100/month insurance (China programmes). Health insurance mandatory.

yes-program-inbound-us-2027-28.about:
The YES programme page (yesprograms.org) lists eligible countries for the spring 2027 semester as Bangladesh, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Egypt, India, Indonesia, Kosovo, Malaysia, North Macedonia and Pakistan. Students pick their country on the site to see local application steps.

For 2027-2028 opportunities the YES pages direct students to discoverflexglobal.org, which hosts the merit-based exchange that builds on YES (FLEX Global itself is listed separately and is not repeated here).

Programs are government-funded, so participants do not pay programme fees. Deadlines are set per country by the local implementing organisation.
yes-program-inbound-us-2027-28.eligibility: High-school students from the eligible countries listed on yesprograms.org (Spring 2027 list: Bangladesh, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Egypt, India, Indonesia, Kosovo, Malaysia, North Macedonia, Pakistan). Georgia and Qatar are not on that list; Georgian students should look at FLEX instead. Age limits are set per country.
how_to_apply: Open yesprograms.org and choose your country under 'Apply to YES'.
Follow the country page for the application form, tests and interviews.
For the 2027-28 year check discoverflexglobal.org for the next call.
yes-program-inbound-us-2027-28.costs: Fully funded by the U.S. Department of State (programme costs, host family placement, school enrolment); personal costs as stated by the local implementing organisation.

yfu-global-exchange-network.about:
YFU (Youth For Understanding) has run exchanges since 1951 and says more than 310,000 young people have taken part. Its network covers more than 45 countries, and each national YFU organisation runs its own application process, fees and scholarships.

Most programmes last one semester or one academic year, with the student living with a host family and attending a local school. Most host countries only ask for some English, though basic skills in the local language help. YFU says over 70% of its member organisations offer partly or fully funded scholarships.

The central YFU site does not list individual deadlines or prices: the student applies through the YFU organisation in their own country (listed on the member organisations page). If your country is not listed, YFU does not currently offer a programme there. Meridian lists several country-level YFU records separately; this entry is the global entry point.
yfu-global-exchange-network.eligibility: Most programmes are for students aged 15 to 18. You apply through the YFU organisation in your own country; if your country has no YFU member, there is no programme there. Rules, language requirements and scholarship eligibility differ by country; check whether citizens of Georgia or Qatar have a YFU partner on the member list.
how_to_apply: Find your national YFU organisation on the member organisations page (about.yfu.org/member-organizations).
Open its website and read the programme, fee and scholarship rules.
Submit the national application and complete any interview or school documents.
Ask about partial or full scholarships when you apply.
yfu-global-exchange-network.costs: Fees are set by each national organisation and are not published centrally. Over 70% of member organisations offer partly or fully funded scholarships.
